newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs off lows after sharp sell-off.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs off lows after sharp sell-off.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures recovered some poise but remained very weak after a sudden sell-off in Friday afternoon trade.
The lead December Euroyen contract was at 98.92 at 0735 GMT after falling as low as 98.89 against its IMM close at 99.03.

Dealers said there was little in the way of fresh news behind the sell-off and players seemed to ignore reports that Moody's Investors Service had downgraded Nippon Credit Bank's bond ratings, a factor that would normally underpin the market.

"We started to see some swap-related selling in Tokyo of a fairly chunky size and that just spooked a thin Euroyen market. Then it was just very technical. There were stops going off all over the place," said a dealer with a European futures house.
He said there was heavy selling by U.S. hedge funds.
"Once we broke 99.01 and then 98.97 (in December Euroyen), it just melted down to 98.89," he added.
Dealers said the contract should find some support around 98.87/88, but a breach of that area would expose it to further weakness to as far as 98.70/72.
A Japanese bank dealer said expectations of firmer interest rates in the cash market ahead of the financial year end on March 31 was also spurring sales of Euroyen futures for hedging purposes.
But he said the market was likely to consolidate and move sideways ahead of the year end and the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly tankan on April 2.
"There's just been a complete turnaround in opinion in the last two days," said the first trader.
He said growing expectations of a U.S. interest rate hike next week were fuelling worries the BOJ might follow suit to prevent a further weakening of the yen.
June JGBs were at 125.43 against their previous 126.09.
